Method of Attack: Delivers banking Trojan and RAT cocktail via malicious Microsoft Word document attachments in phishing emails impersonating eFax messages
Uses ZIP archived XLS Microsoft Excel documents with macros to download and launch Dridex and RMS RAT payloads
Dridex collects credentials from web browsers and exfiltrates them to attacker servers
RMS RAT manages infected computers with capabilities including logging keystrokes, recording from webcam or microphone, transferring files, and manipulating Windows utilities
Dridex uses web injects to steal information typed by victims, bypass security questions and multi-factor authentication, and redirect traffic
Impacted Systems: Windows computers infected via phishing emails with malicious Microsoft Word and Excel documents
Attack Vector: Phishing emails with malicious Microsoft Word document attachments containing ZIP archived XLS files with macros
Indicators of Compromise: ZIP archived XLS Microsoft Excel documents with macros
Command-and-control (C2) server domains for Dridex and RMS RAT
Web inject scripts including some labeled as from Zeus banking trojan
Payload URLs and potential web inject sources listed in Cofense malspam campaign report
